channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: Anthropic's IPO price tag slides toward $1.2 trillion as investors balk after the AI selloff
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Investors are now discussing a $1.2 trillion to $1.3 trillion valuation for Anthropic's IPO, down from as high as $2 trillion in early October, after a sharp AI stock selloff — and the roadshow planned for next week is suddenly in doubt.

item.title: US intelligence memo reportedly links Nvidia's Jensen Huang to alleged Chinese spy
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: US intelligence believes Nvidia chief Jensen Huang was romantically involved with an executive Washington says was recruited by China's spy agency, according to the Financial Times and the New York Times. Nothing is proven — and Congress now wants answers.

item.title: Drive a real browser from your terminal: hands-on with agent-browser, Vercel's CLI for AI agents
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: agent-browser is Vercel's Rust CLI for driving a real browser from the shell: snapshot a page as text, act on element refs, and automate anything a human can click. This guide installs 0.41.2, runs the core loop, extracts live data, drives forms, and wires up MCP — every command verified.

item.title: Octop 1.0.3, hands-on: upgrade your self-hosted AI assistant and build your first expert team
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Tencent's Octop has doubled to 11,753 stars since our first guide, and versions 1.0.2 and 1.0.3 add expert teams, a second-instance cloud bridge, memory you can edit by hand, and an agent MCP gateway. Back up, run octop update, and put the new features to work — every command verified against the current README and release notes.

item.title: GPT-6.1 Terra, hands-on: visual reasoning, structured outputs, and tools with the Responses API
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: OpenAI’s GPT-6.1 Terra is the fast, cheap vision model of the GPT-6 family — $1 per million input tokens, a 1.05M-token context window, and tool calling through the Responses API. This guide makes your first call, feeds it a photo, forces structured JSON out of it, and wires up web search and your own functions — every snippet verified against the official docs.

item.title: Shield AI buys radar maker Echodyne for $5.3B and raises $2.5B at a $28.8B valuation
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Shield AI is buying Kirkland radar maker Echodyne in a deal worth up to $5.3 billion, pairing its autonomy software with the sensors that spot drones — and raising $2.5 billion to pay for it, at a valuation more than double its March mark.

item.title: Your AI agents as chat contacts: hands-on with OpenMausBot, the open-source Grok Bot alternative
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: OpenMausBot turns Claude Code, Codex and Grok into contacts in a chat app — each with its own model, computer and apps. This guide installs the CLI, starts the server, builds a team from a file, and shows exactly where the login gate is. Every command verified.

item.title: A team of 8 built a GTA-style Bangkok in 8 days with its own AI-native engine — and Reddit is checking how much of it the AI really did
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Eight days of in-engine footage shows a GTA-style Bangkok — tuk-tuks, water-cannon trucks and Komodo dragons — built with the team’s own AI-native engine, Oriverse. Reddit’s top comments are equal parts impressed and unconvinced about how much of it the AI really did.

item.title: From one page to a whole crawl: hands-on with Scrapling, the 99K-star Python scraping framework
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Scrapling packs fast HTTP fetching, a stealth browser, adaptive parsing, spiders, a CLI, an MCP server and an agent skill into one Python library. This guide installs 0.5.1, scrapes a real site three ways, crawls 100 quotes into JSON, and wires it into an AI agent — every command verified.

item.title: Federal judge rules Anthropic must face Claude Max subscribers over 20x usage marketing
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A federal judge in California has let a proposed class action against Anthropic go ahead, finding that the company's '5x or 20x more usage than Pro' pitch for its Claude Max plans is 'plausibly misleading' — and that the small print saying the multipliers apply per session may not save it.

item.title: Moonshot publishes Kimi K3.1 Pro’s weights: a 2.8T open model that nearly matches Claude Opus 5.5 on coding
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Moonshot AI has published the full weights of Kimi K3.1 Pro on Hugging Face, keeping its promise from the model’s October launch. The 2.8-trillion-parameter model scores within a point of Claude Opus 5.5 on agentic coding in Moonshot’s own tests — and anyone can now download it, under a license with two conditions for very large operators.

item.title: Run five coding agents in parallel without merge chaos: hands-on with Worktrunk
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Worktrunk turns git worktrees into a one-command workflow for parallel coding agents: create, list, merge, and clean up without ever typing a path. This guide installs v0.81.0, runs two branches through a real merge, and wires up hooks and LLM commit messages — every command verified.

item.title: dsh-superagent: put DeepSeek's proactive coding agent to work on your GitHub repo — hands-on
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: DeepSeek's dsh-superagent watches your GitHub repo, takes requests from people you allow, and opens pull requests on its own. This guide installs it on DeepSeek Harness, gives it its own GitHub account, and runs your first ticket — every command from the project's own docs.

item.title: Text prompt to game asset: hands-on with GLB-3D-Coder, the 4B model that writes Three.js pages and exports real .glb files
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: GLB-3D-Coder is a 4B model that turns a one-line prompt into a Three.js page with an Export GLB button. This guide runs it on a desktop GPU, generates a sword, and validates the exported GLB end to end.

item.title: AMD’s CEO says the company is now “data center first” — gaming is no longer the priority
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Lisa Su told Yahoo Finance that AMD is now a “data center first” company, as third-quarter results showed data-center revenue nearly doubling to $8.5 billion while gaming fell 40% — and PC shipments are forecast to fall by double digits in 2027.

item.title: HiringDesk's Ava: an AI hiring assistant that screens applicants, texts candidates and books interviews
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: HiringDesk.ai launched Ava, an AI hiring assistant that reads applicants, scores them 1–10, texts the qualified ones and books interviews — with plans from $199 a month.

item.title: DeepMind's AI agents found two cracks in legacy 1024-bit RSA — and modern keys are untouched
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Human-guided agents at Google DeepMind found faster ways to forge signatures and factor batches of legacy 1024-bit RSA keys. The results only affect obsolete keys — 2048-bit encryption is untouched — but they show AI stress-testing cryptography far faster than before.

item.title: T3 Code: drive Claude Code, Codex and Cursor from your phone — hands-on with the 50K-star agent control surface
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: T3 Code puts your coding agents behind one server you can drive from a phone, a browser, or a terminal. This guide installs it, wires up a provider, starts a real thread, and links a phone — every command verified.

item.title: Greg Casar calls for a ban on recursive self-improvement after METR finds AI accelerating AI development
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Rep. Greg Casar posted two words — “Ban RSI.” — a day after METR reported that Anthropic’s AI development is running about twice as fast as it would without AI help, with no clear bottleneck in sight.

item.title: An AI-generated musical of tech CEOs singing “We Were Always Blue” went viral after the election — and Reddit’s top comment is a debunk
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: A 113-second AI-generated musical of tech CEOs singing after the election hit r/accelerate on Friday morning and passed 1,700 upvotes — and the thread’s most-upvoted reply is a correction: listen closely, they use autotune.

item.title: Forecast the next 120 candles with Kronos, the foundation model that speaks the language of markets
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Kronos is the first open-source foundation model built for financial candlesticks — and its 4.1M-parameter mini model runs on a CPU. This guide installs it, forecasts 120 days of Bitcoin, and scores the result against what actually happened.

item.title: Four frontier models raced a sailing sim Claude Code built — Gemini 4 Argon won
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: A Reddit user built a 3D sailing simulator with Claude Code, then let Gemini 4 Argon, GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus 5.5 and Qwen3.5-9B race the same course. Argon won — at a fifth of the cost of its nearest rival — but the thread itself is the first to say this was a fun experiment, not a benchmark.

item.title: Six pallets of Nvidia AI hardware worth $11.4 million vanish on the road from Oakland to Texas
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A truck picked up six pallets of Nvidia AI hardware in Oakland on August 29 and never reached Fort Worth. Two months on, police have no suspects and no recovered cargo — and the heist fits a pattern of AI hardware thefts that keeps getting bolder.

item.title: Stanford’s Memorilla squeezes entire conversation histories into 16 memory tokens
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Stanford researchers say their Memorilla system can recall information from entire conversation histories using just 16 memory tokens. An 88-second video of the work has r/singularity debating whether it will ever reach a real product.

item.title: AutoDNA: AI agents ran a DNA lab end to end — humans did the restocking
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Researchers at Shanghai Jiao Tong University built a lab where AI agents design and run DNA experiments from a single typed prompt. In its longest test, the system worked for 203 hours across 11,382 steps — and read the data back without a single error.
